verdict.rationale: FireHydrant gives each incident a dedicated internal status page. All `/fh update` notes and Command Center updates post there, and viewers need no auth or license. AI summaries are open to the whole Slack workspace and can be tailored by Audience, so stakeholders can follow structured updates without joining the war room. Missing for 10: any documented self-service subscription mechanism (e.g., subscribing to an incident or status page for notifications), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, internal stakeholders get structured incident updates they can subscribe to, without joining the war room

citations.quote: All incident notes/updates posted via Slack (`/fh update`) or via Command Center are posted to the Internal Status Page
For public (to your organization) incidents, these internal status pages do not require auth or a FireHydrant license to view.
With our new Audiences feature, summaries can now be tailored to meet the specific needs of different stakeholder groups.
Universal Access: Available to everyone in your Slack workspace, they don't need a FireHydrant account.
